clue.text: Yours truly's limited by nasty antisocial act is getting used to things

indicators.note: being limited by something is being hemmed in by it, so the setter's own letters sit inside the rearranged phrase
something nasty is twisted out of its proper shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: 'yours truly is' is I'M

explanation.surface: A setter confesses to being caught up in some unpleasant antisocial behaviour while adapting to new surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges ANTISOCIAL ACT; 'limited by' puts I'M (yours truly is) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclimatisation is the process of adjusting to a new climate or environment, which is getting accustomed to things.

clue.text: Having received audible jeer, escaped totally exhausted

indicators.note: the word for escaped takes in the jeer, so it holds those letters inside

parts.note: fled means escaped
a razz, or raspberry, is a jeer you can hear, a rude noise of derision

explanation.surface: Someone flees after being jeered and ends up worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: To razz is to blow a raspberry, the derisive noise; it goes inside FLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Frazzled is an informal word for being completely worn out, nerves shredded by strain.

clue.text: Record year with help having been set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, read from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A year's record is put together with some assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Write YR then AID and read the whole upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary is a daily record of events kept by its writer.

clue.text: Prisoners, kind to get locked in as mates

indicators.note: the word for kind is shut inside the prisoners, as a jailed person is locked in

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners
a sort is a kind

explanation.surface: Jailbirds of a certain type become locked up together as companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Consorts are partners or companions, especially spouses, so mates fits as a plural noun.

clue.text: Sends up meals to two opponents at table

parts.note: teas are light afternoon or evening meals
at the bridge table East and South are opposing players, E and S

explanation.surface: Someone serves meals to a pair of opponents seated at a table, perhaps a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are North, South, East and West; East and South play against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone up is to mock them playfully, which is what one does when one teases.

clue.text: Graduate makes a case, penning short excuse

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as animals in a pen, so the box holds the excuse inside

parts.note: a crate is a case or packing box

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: an alibi is an excuse

explanation.surface: A university graduate builds an argument while writing a brief excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graduate' looks like a noun for a degree-holder; here it is the verb, to mark an instrument with a scale. 'a case' is one leaf: a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: To graduate an instrument is to mark it with a measuring scale, which is what calibrating does.

clue.text: I travel into place to have a hearty meal

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces goes inside the word for place

parts.note: to put is to place
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A traveller arrives somewhere to enjoy a big meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig out is informal for eating greedily, gorging on a large meal.

clue.text: Wild gang proceeds on a run hampered by stuff carried

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An unruly gang heads off on a run, slowed by the loot they are carrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like part of the gang's escape, but it begins the definition: a race where runners are slowed by an egg carried on a spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: In this school sports day race, competitors run while balancing an egg on a spoon, which hinders their pace.

clue.text: Hormone? My mood is being restricted

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

indicators.note: is is restricted by being enclosed within the word for mood

parts.note: tone means mood, as in the tone of a gathering

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if a hormone explains why their mood feels held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation, not the possessive: COR, as in 'Cor blimey'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cortisone is a steroid hormone produced by the adrenal cortex and used to treat inflammation.

clue.text: Doing brilliantly, confronting leader to be deposed

indicators.note: the leading letter is removed, as a leader is ousted

parts.note: facing means confronting

explanation.surface: A rebel succeeds by standing up to a leader who is about to be overthrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Acing something is doing it perfectly, as in aceing an exam or serving an ace in tennis.

clue.text: Man given new life to be idle, mostly before a short dash

indicators.note: places the idling word ahead of the rest
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to laze is to be idle

indicators.note: short means docked of the final letter

parts.note: a rush is a dash

explanation.surface: A lazy man rouses himself for a quick sprint and is reinvigorated.
explanation.walkthrough: LAZE loses its last letter, then A, then RUSH loses its last.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospel of John, Jesus raises Lazarus from the dead, restoring him to life.

clue.text: Philosopher bites back, cross about article

indicators.note: back means read backwards, so the word for bites is turned round

parts.note: nips are little bites

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the hybrid's name runs backwards

parts.note: a zo (or dzo) is a cross between a yak and a domestic cow
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A cross philosopher snaps back over some article.
explanation.walkthrough: The ZO, a yak-cow hybrid, is a crossword regular; reversed it gives OZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a seventeenth-century Dutch rationalist thinker, author of the Ethics.

clue.text: Welsh town's fashion, not posh

indicators.note: not says the letter for posh is left out

parts.note: to mould is to fashion or shape
U means upper-class, posh, as in 'U and non-U'

explanation.surface: A Welsh town's style is described as unpretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: MOLD is the county town of Flintshire in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Mold is a market town in Flintshire, north-east Wales, a real place name.

clue.text: Defeated female, corrosive influence getting told off

parts.note: rust corrodes metal
to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.surface: A woman is reprimanded for being a bad influence.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE meaning to scold is old-fashioned but crossword-common.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that are frustrated are thwarted or foiled, which is being defeated.

clue.text: Illness? One must get up minimally, obeying instructions

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up is rising; minimally means by just one place

parts.note: a complaint is an illness or ailment
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sick person is told they must get out of bed briefly, if they are following doctor's orders.
explanation.walkthrough: In COMPLAINT the I moves up one place to sit before the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone compliant does as they are told, acquiescing and conforming to rules.

clue.text: It's dull outside, terribly

indicators.note: terribly means very badly, so these letters are badly scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the weather out of doors is dreadfully dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious means boring and monotonous, lacking interest.

clue.text: Stones number one track changes here

parts.note: pits are fruit stones
top means first, number one

explanation.surface: It reads like the Rolling Stones' chart-topping single, with a hint at editing software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track changes' looks like a word-processor feature; it is where tyres are changed on a race track.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pit stop in motor racing, a car pulls off the circuit to change tyres and refuel.

clue.text: What garden centres sell? There's fuss over British Standards

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sits over the next

parts.note: pother is an old word for fuss or commotion
BS is the abbreviation for British Standards

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders about garden centre stock and frets about safety standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Potherbs are herbs grown for cooking, plants a garden centre would stock.

clue.text: Old garment no good? Smart and hot!

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: a toga was the garment of ancient Rome
to smart is to sting

explanation.surface: Someone appraises an outfit as tired, yet stylish and attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' and 'hot' both look like fashion praise; smart is the verb for sting, hot is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasting means very warm, as in a toasting fire or toasting hands.

clue.text: Awfully cosy when meeting power, hard workers who toady

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Cosy flatterers fawning on those with power, though they claim to toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophants are flatterers, people who fawn on the powerful to win favour.

clue.text: Two companions outside historic city chapel?

indicators.note: the companions stand outside, enclosing the old city

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour; two of them give CH twice
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Two friends standing outside an old city's chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a chapel is only one example of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small place of Christian worship, so a kind of church.

clue.text: One bit of a plant another duck's destroyed

indicators.note: the duck being destroyed means it vanishes from the word

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, hence O

explanation.surface: A second duck has wrecked part of a plant in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The anther is the part of a flower's stamen that holds pollen.

clue.text: Old flyers going round in game

indicators.note: going round means turning to face the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: Veteran pilots circle around during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is an old gambling card game, once popular in the American West.

clue.text: 3 writer? Yes, working through pages

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An author agrees while busy leafing through pages.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' refers to the answer at 3 down, DIARY: Samuel Pepys is the great English diarist.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys kept the most famous English diary, recording 1660s London life.

clue.text: Sightseer: gentleman about to be taken in by spiv?

indicators.note: the reversed gentleman goes inside the spiv's word

parts.note: a spiv is a British flashy petty crook; a tout sells tickets on the black market

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the title runs backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title of a gentleman or knight

explanation.surface: A visitor, a gentleman, is about to be duped by a wide boy, as the question mark suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is a British slang word for a flashy black-market dealer; a tout, selling tickets at inflated prices, is a fair match.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is a person travelling for pleasure, seeing the sights of a place.

clue.text: First woman almost to register as competitive rider

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis
to enter is to register, as for a competition

explanation.surface: The first woman nearly signs up for a competition as a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse or rider taking part in eventing, the equestrian three-day competition.

clue.text: Love to examine old language

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, hence O
to scan is to examine

explanation.surface: Someone loves examining an ancient tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscan was an Italic language of ancient southern Italy, replaced by Latin.

clue.text: Incomer by ground that has yet to be developed

definitions.text: that has yet to be developed

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newcomer passes by some land awaiting development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a plot of land; it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Embryonic describes something at a rudimentary stage, still to grow and mature.
